children: Joby Aviation (JOBY) shares fell nearly 8% in morning trading Friday, touching $5.3 and setting a new 52-week low as investor concerns weighed on the electric aircraft developer.

The stock has lost about 65% of its value over the past year and now trades more than 70% below its 52-week peak of $18.77. The latest decline adds to pressure on a company working to establish its position in the emerging electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft market.

Recent business developments have offered some support. Joby reported $38.6 million in second-quarter 2026 revenue, compared with $24.2 million in the first quarter. Its Blade passenger business contributed $36.2 million, reflecting increased activity in the air mobility segment.

The company has also agreed to acquire defense technology firm Resonant Sciences for about $500 million, expanding its exposure to defense-related work. However, the stock's continued slide suggests investors remain cautious about its commercial prospects and execution risks.

H.C. Wainwright maintained a Buy rating with an $18 price target, while Cantor Fitzgerald retained a Neutral stance. Investors will be watching progress on commercialization, funding needs and the integration of the planned acquisition as Joby seeks to regain market confidence.

title: Joby Aviation Shares Sink 8% as Stock Hits 52-Week Low
